definition: Ancillary services used to hold grid frequency at 60 hertz by responding to automatic control signals that raise (reg up) or lower (reg down) a generator's output.
core_idea: Regulation resources must be able to respond to automated dispatch signals very quickly (about a minute) to fine-tune output and keep grid frequency steady.
key_points: Regulation Up: generator responds to signals to increase production, typically within about a minute.
Regulation Down: generator responds to signals to decrease production, typically within about a minute.
Regulation services are tied directly to maintaining 60 hertz frequency on the grid.
Exact performance requirements vary by power grid/ISO.
relationships: Directly tied to frequency response concept.
